correctness.rationale: The proof reduces all dimensions to independent difference-span cosets, classifies all six-point affine shapes (ranks 3, 4 with a 4-circuit, 4 with a 6-circuit, and 5), computes the two 4-dimensional graph possibilities and proves all maximal length-five distance-three binary codes have size 2 or 4. Exact counts 16/120 are obtained analytically by Hamming-weight cases and incidence counting. The labeled six-subset counts follow by finite affine-subspace and group orbit formulas. Independently implemented maximal-clique and direct-combination algorithms reproduce the local histograms, and complete enumeration of the 169911 normalized six-subsets in the five-cube reproduces the census. All domains and boundaries are stated; no finite experiment is extrapolated to the arbitrary-dimensional theorem.

The earlier group-stability classification and known 2-versus-4 simplex example do not state these polynomial multiplicities, the other three case counts, or the six-subset labeled census. Full accessible principal sources and targeted terminology/stronger-implication searches were compared. Absolute historical priority is not established; coding-table coverage of some component counts remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: Complete exact generating polynomials for all six-point supports provide a natural refinement of the recent finite-group subfactor/index-stability problems: not merely which group or support is stable, but precisely how many maximal disjoint-translate packings exist at every size. Four intrinsic affine geometries yield different local enumerations and a full distribution in any ambient dimension. The rank-five simplex multiplicity is only one case; rank-four geometry and the complete labeled \(\mathbb F_2^5\) support census furnish a structural classification and useful reproducible benchmarks. Prior known extremal sizes are not presented as the novel contribution.
